national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Provincial (Quebec): Revenu Québec, clicSÉQUR Entreprises portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca). Corporate registry: Corporations Canada (federal) and Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), which issues the 9-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act; obtain the NEQ from REQ. Step 2: Apply to CRA for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST program account (RT prefix) via Business Registration Online or Form RC1. Step 3: Register for QST with Revenu Québec (Form LM-1-V or clicSÉQUR Entreprises using the NEQ); add payroll accounts (QPIP, CNESST, EHT) if staff are hired. Step 4: Foreign non-resident entities register through CRA's International Tax Services Office (Form RC1 with non-resident identification) and through Revenu Québec's non-resident registration desk; non-resident suppliers carrying on business in Canada must register irrespective of the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: Canadian-resident corporation taxed on worldwide income under the Income Tax Act, Part I, and the Quebec Taxation Act; non-resident corporation taxed only on Canadian-source income. No pass-through or check-the-box election exists. Federal general corporate rate 15% (after provincial abatement); Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction reduces the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Quebec general rate 11.5%; Quebec small business rate 5.0%. DTC cosmetics retail constitutes active business income eligible for the small business deduction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime is available. Statutory elections: (i) ITA s. 85 rollover on transfers to/from a corporation; (ii) s. 83 capital dividend election; (iii) s. 110.6 capital gains deduction reserve; (iv) s. 45(2)/(3) change-of-use election for real property; (v) s. 39(4) capital property disposition election; (vi) s. 216 election for non-resident rental/timber income; (vii) anti-hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.4–18.5 countering double non-taxation through entity- or instrument-mismatch arrangements; (viii) Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation (EIFEL) elections under ITA s. 18.2 effective for taxation years beginning on or after October 1, 2023, restricting cross-border interest deductibility.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT system: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% under the Excise Tax Act, Part IX, and provincial Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.5% under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax; combined effective rate 14.5% on taxable supplies delivered into Quebec. Cross-province DTC sales follow destination-based GST/HST rates (Ontario 13%, British Columbia 12%, Alberta 5% GST-only).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) in any single calendar quarter or in any four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier exemption). QST: identical CAD 30,000 threshold based on taxable supplies made in Quebec. Non-resident suppliers with a Canadian establishment or carrying on business in Canada must register regardless of the threshold; non-residents supplying only zero-rated goods or services are exempt from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), API clearance, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. E-invoicing is voluntary but standardized under the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Framework (Peppol BIS 3.0). CRA accepts paper, PDF, and EDI records; Revenu Québec requires invoices to show the NEQ/BN, vendor identification, date, description, and a separate breakdown of GST and QST amounts. Shopify Payments and PayPal receipts must satisfy ETA s. 223 and QST Act s. 373 content rules; DTC merchants must maintain an integrated audit trail in their accounting systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods is zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 5, provided physical exportation is substantiated. Export of services to a non-resident is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 7–9 where the non-resident is outside Canada at the time of performance and the supply is not an excepted supply (services to a Canadian establishment, advertising directed at the Canadian market). QST mirrors zero-rating under the QST Act, Schedule I. For ISIC 4791 DTC cosmetics retail, shipments delivered to foreign addresses qualify if supported by carrier waybills and export declarations; the registrant concurrently claims full GST input tax credits and QST input tax refunds. Domestic shipments to other Canadian provinces are taxable under place-of-supply rules at the destination province's rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice (Canada Customs Invoice format) with full HS classification of cosmetics and unit values
Canadian Export Declaration filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000, or documented low-value exemption for shipments of CAD 2,000 or less
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) naming the DTC entity as shipper and a foreign consignee, evidencing physical export from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 confirmation, or PayPal/Shopify Payments settlement ledger evidencing foreign-currency collection from the overseas buyer
Packing list, third-party carrier tracking history, and customs broker acknowledgments forming the complete export evidence bundle
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within 4 years (Revenu Québec: 3 years under the Tax Administration Act); extended to 7 years for misrepresentation, neglect, or omission. Failure of export documentation causes re-characterization of the sale as taxable, retrospective clawback of input tax credits/refunds, and compound daily interest at prescribed rates. Civil penalties: gross-negligence penalty of 50% of additional tax (ITA s. 163(2); ETA s. 285; Quebec TAA s. 1051) and false-statement penalties of 5%–25%. Criminal exposure: tax evasion under ITA s. 239 and ETA s. 327 carries fines of 50%–200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years. Customs Act administrative monetary penalties apply for missing export declarations. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; 180 days is the conventional audit benchmark for demonstrating timely foreign-currency settlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) under the Bank of Canada Act; prudential banking supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); payment system oversight by Payments Canada (Canadian Payments Association) and the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) regime administered by the Bank of Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII; no exchange control regime has existed since the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951. Profit remittances (dividends, interest, royalties) are freely repatriable in any convertible currency and are subject only to standard Income Tax Act withholding taxes and transfer-pricing documentation, without prior central bank or ministerial approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or barter-control requirement for export receipts. A Quebec-based cosmetics exporter may retain and deploy foreign-currency proceeds freely in domestic or offshore operating accounts, subject only to ordinary anti-money-laundering (FINTRAC) record-keeping and reporting duties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium with strict legal constraints. Offshore or Canadian fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) may be used as auxiliary collection and disbursement channels, but they are not Schedule I banks; they operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and are subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) registration. They cannot provide regulatory capital escrow, LVTS settlement, or confirmed letters of credit. For a Quebec beauty DTC entity, use such EMIs only for low-value card settlement and retain a Tier 1 bank relationship for core treasury, FX, and clearing rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for a Canadian-controlled online retail corporation if the directors hold verifiable Canadian identity records; however, most Quebec Tier 1 banks require a virtual or physical interview for non-face-to-face account activation, particularly for any authorized signatory who is a non-resident. For the CA_CORP entity, at least one director or the corporate secretary must complete a live video interview and provide notarized identification if the company is opened remotely. Where the entity's ultimate beneficial owner resides outside Canada, full-UBO verification and a physical branch meeting at a Montreal location are commonly required as an enhanced due diligence measure under FINTRAC guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner structure opaque or nominee shareholders with less than full tax-residence documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) enterprise extract; Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) or Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) certificate of incorporation; articles, by-laws, and unanimous shareholder agreement; complete register of directors, officers, and shareholders; signed UBO declaration with passport copies and CRA tax-residency confirmation letters (or equivalent foreign tax authority certificates).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business purpose mismatch between incorporation documents and bank-entered profile (e.g., cosmetics retail versus payment-processing or money-services activity).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended articles of incorporation expressly stating online retail sale of cosmetics and personal care products; Government of Canada Business Number (BN) and applicable CRA program accounts (Payroll, GST/HST, Import/Export); REQ registration with correct NAICS 456120 / ISIC 4791 classification; detailed business plan and website evidence confirming a goods-based DTC model with no third-party money transmission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First inbound capital injection originates from a foreign shareholder or a jurisdiction deemed non-cooperative by the FATF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital subscription agreement and board resolution authorizing the share issuance; sworn source-of-wealth declaration for the shareholder; original bank statements from the originating financial institution covering 6 months of activity; tax invoice or letter of no-tax-liability where the shareholder is a trading company; confirmation that the transfer will be executed via SWIFT MT103 with full originator/beneficiary transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cross-border trade disbursements or round-tripping triggers a bank Transaction Monitoring (TM) alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders, supplier invoices, and shipping documents including bill of lading / air waybill; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) customs entry or export declaration referencing HS code 3304; three-way matching worksheet; distribution agreement and commission schedule; statement from the chief financial officer explaining trade-cycle timing and expected FX conversion patterns.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For shareholder equity contribution into CA_CORP, remit via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the CAD-denominated operational or capital escrow account at a Montreal Schedule I bank, using purpose code 'Capital Contribution' (OBI field: 'Share Capital / Equity Injection'). CAD leg settles via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) at Payments Canada in real time; USD funds may be held in a USD clearing account and converted to CAD via spot or forward rate at the beneficiary bank. All inbound injections must be supported by corporate resolutions, and the Canadian recipient must file any applicable CRA Form T1134 (foreign affiliate or shareholder reporting) and remain below the Investment Canada Act threshold for FINA review (CAD 4.14 billion for non-state-owned WTO investors in 2024).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for supplier payments, duties, and logistics are executed via SWIFT MT103 over LVTS (CAD) or SWIFT/CHIPS (USD), with a 1-2 business-day finality window. For high-value supplier contracts exceeding CAD 50,000, use standby or commercial letters of credit governed by UCP 600, advised through a Schedule I bank; for recurring retail-related disbursements (e.g., Shopify settlement payouts, payroll, and CBSA duty deposits), use Payments Canada's automated clearing (ACSS) for CAD debits/credits and a USD concentration account at a U.S. correspondent bank to minimize cross-border conversion costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (up to 36 months tenor) with a Schedule I bank under ISDA/CADAR corporate master agreements
FX Swaps and Rollovers for aligned inter-month liquidity
Cross-Currency Swaps (CAD/USD or CAD/EUR) for long-term balance-sheet hedging of the beauty retail import cycle
Zero-Cost Collars (risk reversals) to cap adverse CAD movement while retaining upside; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted or necessary for CAD given full convertibility

USD 188) for filings older than one year; failure to file for two consecutive annual returns leads to a published Notice of Intent to Dissolve in the Canada Gazette and eventual administrative dissolution and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c. P-44.1) - annual statutory reconfirmation of the corporation's directors, principal establishment, place of administration and ultimate beneficial ownership particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation / initial registration in Quebec, every year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 10 per day, generally capped at approximately CAD 300 (approx. USD 225); sustained default for several years triggers radiation (cancellation) of the enterprise's registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (T2) with financial statements and applicable tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the fiscal period (e.g., June 30 of the following year for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delay (maximum 12 months); prescribed interest on outstanding balances; possible CRA enforcement measures including demands, garnishment and suspension of tax-related registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return (CO-17) with related provincial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the fiscal period (e.g., June 30 of the following year for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid provincial tax plus 1% per complete month of delay (maximum 12 months); interest at the prescribed rate; Revenu Quebec may issue compliance demands and escalate collection measures.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction reduces federal rate to 9% on first CAD 500,000; Quebec small business deduction reduces provincial rate to 3.2% on first CAD 500,000; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Quebec CO-17; filed via CRA's NETFILE or third-party software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide revenue; non-resident corporations with Canadian business income must file.
Deductible expenses must be reasonable and supported by documentation.
Compute after deducting expenses and applying loss carryovers.
Apply federal rates and credits; non-residents may be subject to Part I tax on Canadian-source income.
Apply Quebec tax rates and credits; file separate CO-17 with Revenu Québec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty 10% plus 2% per month; interest on late payments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (Form NR-301) to the Canadian payer before payment; the payer must withhold at the treaty rate if satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory, reduced to 10% under many treaties (e.g., US); Interest: 25% statutory, often reduced to 0% for arm's length interest under treaties (e.g., US).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for services; CAD 5 million for other transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) not applicable in Canada; general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income or overstatement of deductions to evade tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% of tax evaded; criminal prosecution with fines up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they failed to withhold or remit; civil restitution and potential travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporation without economic substance, used to artificially shift profits or avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, penalties up to 50% of tax avoided
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for tax debts if they knowingly participated in sham arrangements; civil penalties and potential criminal charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML compliance, suspicious transaction reporting, or record-keeping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal penalties for money laundering up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned for knowingly failing to comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
